```plato
//==
// # Quantities
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Dynamic units
//  - Electromagnetic quantities
//  - Geometric quantities
//  - Kinematic quantities
//  - Material-response and flow quantities
//  - Mechanical quantities
//  - Photometric and radiometric quantities
//  - Thermal and chemical quantities

//==
// # Dynamic units
//
// Unit systems resolved at runtime rather than by type (file import, UI,
// scientific data). A `Dimension` is the exponent vector over the seven SI base
// dimensions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SI_base_unit), a `UnitOfMeasure`
// pairs a dimension with an affine conversion to SI, and a `DynamicQuantity` is
// an amount tagged with such a unit.

// Exponents of the seven SI base dimensions
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimensional_analysis). A dimensionless value
// has all zeros.
type Dimension
{
    LengthPower: Integer;
    MassPower: Integer;
    TimePower: Integer;
    CurrentPower: Integer;
    TemperaturePower: Integer;
    AmountPower: Integer;
    LuminosityPower: Integer;
}

// A named unit of measure with a conversion to SI: si = value * ScaleToSI + OffsetToSI
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_of_measurement).
type UnitOfMeasure
{
    Name: String;
    Symbol: String;
    Dimension: Dimension;
    ScaleToSI: Number;
    OffsetToSI: Number;
}

// A runtime-typed quantity: an amount tagged with a unit value.
type DynamicQuantity
{
    Amount: Number;
    Unit: UnitOfMeasure;
}

//==
// # Electromagnetic quantities
//
// Current and charge, potential difference, and the three passive circuit
// elements - resistance, capacitance, inductance
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electromagnetism). Repetition rate, which
// electrical work also needs, is `Frequency` in the kinematic section.

// Electric current, stored in amperes
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_current).
type ElectricCurrent implements IQuantity { Amperes: Number; }

// Electric charge, stored in coulombs
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_charge).
type ElectricCharge implements IQuantity { Coulombs: Number; }

// Electric potential, stored in volts (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voltage).
type Voltage implements IQuantity { Volts: Number; }

// Electrical resistance, stored in ohms
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_resistance_and_conductance).
type Resistance implements IQuantity { Ohms: Number; }

// Electrical capacitance, stored in farads
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capacitance).
type Capacitance implements IQuantity { Farads: Number; }

// Electrical inductance, stored in henries
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inductance).
type Inductance implements IQuantity { Henries: Number; }

//==
// # Geometric quantities
//
// The quantities of extent and shape: angle and solid angle, the length / area
// / volume ladder, and the two reciprocal-length measures (wavenumber and
// curvature). Each stores its canonical SI unit in the field name; rates of
// change of these live in the kinematic section.

// A planar angle, stored in radians (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angle).
type Angle implements IQuantity { Radians: Number; }

// A solid angle, stored in steradians (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid_angle).
type SolidAngle implements IQuantity { Steradians: Number; }

// A spatial distance, stored in meters (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length).
type Length implements IQuantity { Meters: Number; }

// A surface measure, stored in square meters (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area).
type Area implements IQuantity { SquareMeters: Number; }

// A spatial volume, stored in cubic meters (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volume).
type Volume implements IQuantity { CubicMeters: Number; }

// Spatial frequency (cycles per meter); the reciprocal of wavelength
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavenumber).
type WaveNumber implements IQuantity { CyclesPerMeter: Number; }

// Curvature, stored as reciprocal meters (1/radius)
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curvature).
type Curvature implements IQuantity { PerMeter: Number; }

//==
// # Kinematic quantities
//
// Rates of change with respect to time, linear and angular, plus repetition
// rate (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinematics). Motion is described without
// reference to the forces producing it; those are the mechanical quantities.

// Rate of change of position, stored in meters per second
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed).
type Speed implements IQuantity { MetersPerSecond: Number; }

// Rate of change of speed, stored in meters per second squared
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acceleration).
type Acceleration implements IQuantity { MetersPerSecondSquared: Number; }

// Rate of change of acceleration, stored in meters per second cubed
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerk_(physics)).
type Jerk implements IQuantity { MetersPerSecondCubed: Number; }

// Rate of rotation, stored in radians per second
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_velocity).
type AngularVelocity implements IQuantity { RadiansPerSecond: Number; }

// Rate of change of angular velocity, stored in radians per second squared
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_acceleration).
type AngularAcceleration implements IQuantity { RadiansPerSecondSquared: Number; }

// Repetition rate, stored in hertz (cycles per second)
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency).
type Frequency implements IQuantity { Hertz: Number; }

//==
// # Material-response and flow quantities
//
// How a body or a fluid answers an applied load: pressure and strain, the
// spring / damper pair, the two viscosities, and mass and volume flow rates
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continuum_mechanics). These are the constants
// simulation code reaches for once the mechanical quantities describe the load
// itself.

// Force per area, stored in pascals. Also used for stress
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pressure).
type Pressure implements IQuantity { Pascals: Number; }
```
